name: Law of Demand
expr: concept: as price falls, quantity demanded rises, ceteris paribus

name: Law of Supply
expr: concept: as price rises, quantity supplied rises, ceteris paribus

name: Linear Demand Function
expr: Qd = a − bP

name: Linear Supply Function
expr: Qs = c + dP

name: Market Equilibrium Condition
expr: Qd = Qs

name: Equilibrium Quantity
expr: Q* = a − bP*

name: Consumer Surplus
expr: CS = ½ × Q × (Pmax − Pe)

name: Producer Surplus
expr: PS = ½ × Q × (Pe − Pmin)

name: Total Surplus
expr: TS = CS + PS

name: Excess Demand
expr: ED = Qd − Qs, when Qd > Qs at given price

name: Excess Supply
expr: ES = Qs − Qd, when Qs > Qd at given price

name: Cobweb Model
expr: concept: cyclical price/quantity adjustment when supply reacts to past prices

name: Giffen Good
expr: concept: a good whose quantity demanded rises as price rises

name: Veblen Good
expr: concept: a good demanded more as price rises due to status/prestige

name: Normal Good
expr: concept: demand rises as income rises

name: Inferior Good
expr: concept: demand falls as income rises

name: Substitute Goods
expr: concept: rise in price of one raises demand for the other

name: Complementary Goods
expr: concept: rise in price of one lowers demand for the other

name: Market Demand
expr: Qm = ΣQi (sum of all individual demands)

name: Market Supply
expr: Qs(market) = ΣQi (sum of all individual supplies)

name: Opportunity Cost
expr: concept: value of the next best alternative forgone

name: Production Possibility Frontier
expr: concept: curve showing maximum combinations of two goods producible with given resources

name: Circular Flow of Income
expr: concept: continuous flow of income and expenditure between households and firms

name: Scarcity
expr: concept: limited resources relative to unlimited wants

name: Price Elasticity of Demand
expr: Ed = (%ΔQd) / (%ΔP)

name: Price Elasticity (Point Method)
expr: Ed = (dQ/dP) × (P/Q)

name: Income Elasticity of Demand
expr: Ey = (%ΔQd) / (%ΔIncome)

name: Cross Elasticity of Demand
expr: Exy = (%ΔQx) / (%ΔPy)

name: Price Elasticity of Supply
expr: Es = (%ΔQs) / (%ΔP)

name: Perfectly Elastic Demand
expr: concept: Ed = ∞, horizontal demand curve

name: Perfectly Inelastic Demand
expr: concept: Ed = 0, vertical demand curve

name: Unitary Elastic Demand
expr: concept: Ed = 1

name: Elastic Demand
expr: concept: Ed > 1

name: Inelastic Demand
expr: concept: Ed < 1

name: Total Revenue Test
expr: concept: relates change in TR to elasticity when price changes

name: TR–Elastic Demand Relation
expr: when demand is elastic, TR falls as price rises

name: TR–Inelastic Demand Relation
expr: when demand is inelastic, TR rises as price rises

name: Advertising Elasticity of Demand
expr: Ea = (%ΔQd) / (%ΔAdvertising Expenditure)

name: Elasticity of Substitution
expr: σ = %Δ(K/L) / %Δ(MRTS)

name: Engel's Law
expr: concept: proportion of income spent on food falls as income rises

name: Elasticity and Slope Relation
expr: concept: elasticity varies along a straight-line demand curve even though slope is constant

name: Elasticity of Demand for Necessities
expr: concept: typically Ed < 1

name: Elasticity of Demand for Luxuries
expr: concept: typically Ed > 1

name: Short-run vs Long-run Elasticity
expr: concept: elasticity of demand/supply is generally greater in the long run

name: Derived Demand Elasticity
expr: concept: elasticity of demand for an input depends on elasticity of demand for the final good

name: Elasticity of Labor Demand
expr: EL = (%ΔLabor Demanded) / (%ΔWage)

name: Elasticity of Labor Supply
expr: ELs = (%ΔHours Supplied) / (%ΔWage)

name: Tax Incidence and Elasticity
expr: concept: relatively inelastic side of the market bears more of a tax burden

name: Marginal Utility
expr: MU = ΔTU / ΔQ

name: Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility
expr: concept: MU falls as more units of a good are consumed

name: Utility Maximization Rule
expr: MUx / Px = MUy / Py

name: Marginal Rate of Substitution
expr: MRS = MUx / MUy

name: Indifference Curve
expr: concept: locus of combinations of two goods giving equal utility

name: Budget Line
expr: Income = PxQx + PyQy

name: Budget Line Slope
expr: slope = −Px / Py

name: Substitution Effect
expr: concept: change in quantity demanded due to relative price change alone

name: Income Effect
expr: concept: change in quantity demanded due to change in real income

name: Total Price Effect
expr: Total Effect = Substitution Effect + Income Effect

name: Marshallian Consumer Surplus
expr: CS = area under demand curve above price, up to quantity purchased

name: Cardinal Utility Approach
expr: concept: utility is measurable in absolute units (utils)

name: Ordinal Utility Approach
expr: concept: consumers can only rank bundles, not measure utility numerically

name: Revealed Preference Theory
expr: concept: consumer preferences inferred from observed choices

name: Compensating Variation
expr: concept: income adjustment needed to keep utility constant after a price change

name: Equivalent Variation
expr: concept: income change equivalent in effect to a proposed price change

name: Marginal Utility of Money
expr: concept: change in utility from one additional unit of money income

name: Diminishing MRS
expr: concept: MRS falls as more of one good is substituted for another along an indifference curve

name: Corner Solution
expr: concept: optimum where consumer spends entire income on one good

name: Slutsky Equation
expr: ∂x/∂p = substitution effect − x(∂x/∂m) (income effect)

name: Expected Utility
expr: EU = ΣPi × Ui

name: Certainty Equivalent
expr: concept: guaranteed amount a risk-averse person accepts instead of an uncertain outcome

name: Risk Premium (Consumer Theory)
expr: RP = Expected Value − Certainty Equivalent

name: Income Consumption Curve
expr: concept: locus of consumer equilibrium points as income changes, prices constant

name: Price Consumption Curve
expr: concept: locus of consumer equilibrium points as one price changes, income constant

name: Average Product
expr: AP = TP / L

name: Marginal Product
expr: MP = ΔTP / ΔL

name: Law of Variable Proportions
expr: concept: as one input increases, other fixed, output first rises then falls (short-run)

name: Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns
expr: concept: MP of a variable input eventually declines as more of it is used

name: Production Function
expr: Q = f(K, L)

name: Cobb-Douglas Production Function
expr: Q = A·K^α·L^β

name: Returns to Scale
expr: concept: how output changes when all inputs are increased proportionally

name: Increasing Returns to Scale
expr: concept: output rises more than proportionally to input increase

name: Constant Returns to Scale
expr: concept: output rises exactly proportionally to input increase

name: Decreasing Returns to Scale
expr: concept: output rises less than proportionally to input increase

name: Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution
expr: MRTS = MPL / MPK

name: Isoquant
expr: concept: curve showing combinations of two inputs producing the same output

name: Isocost Line
expr: C = wL + rK

name: Producer Equilibrium (Least Cost Combination)
expr: MPL/w = MPK/r

name: Expansion Path
expr: concept: locus of producer equilibrium points as output level changes

name: Economies of Scale
expr: concept: long-run average cost falls as output increases

name: Diseconomies of Scale
expr: concept: long-run average cost rises as output increases

name: Total Factor Productivity
expr: TFP = Output / (Weighted combination of all inputs)

name: Elasticity of Output
expr: Eq = %ΔQ / %Δ(all inputs)

name: Value of Marginal Product
expr: VMP = MP × P

name: Marginal Revenue Product
expr: MRP = MP × MR

name: Technical Efficiency
expr: concept: producing maximum output from a given set of inputs

name: Allocative Efficiency
expr: concept: producing the combination of goods most valued by society, P = MC

name: Leontief Production Function
expr: Q = min(K/a, L/b)

name: Euler's Theorem in Production
expr: Q = MPL·L + MPK·K, under constant returns to scale

name: Total Cost
expr: TC = TFC + TVC

name: Average Fixed Cost
expr: AFC = TFC / Q

name: Average Variable Cost
expr: AVC = TVC / Q

name: Average Total Cost
expr: ATC = TC / Q

name: Marginal Cost
expr: MC = ΔTC / ΔQ

name: Total Cost Function (Cubic form)
expr: TC = a + bQ + cQ² + dQ³

name: Break-even Point
expr: condition: TR = TC

name: Break-even Quantity
expr: Q = FC / (P − AVC)

name: Shutdown Point
expr: concept: firm shuts down in short run when P < minimum AVC

name: Economies of Scope
expr: concept: cost saving from producing multiple products together vs separately

name: Learning Curve Effect
expr: concept: average cost falls as cumulative output/experience rises

name: Explicit Cost
expr: concept: actual money payment made by a firm for inputs

name: Implicit Cost
expr: concept: opportunity cost of resources the firm owns and uses itself

name: Economic Cost
expr: Economic Cost = Explicit Cost + Implicit Cost

name: Accounting Profit
expr: Accounting Profit = TR − Explicit Cost

name: Economic Profit
expr: Economic Profit = TR − (Explicit Cost + Implicit Cost)

name: Normal Profit
expr: concept: minimum profit needed to keep a firm in its current business, economic profit = 0

name: Sunk Cost
expr: concept: cost already incurred and irrecoverable, irrelevant to future decisions

name: Marginal Cost and Marginal Product Relation
expr: MC = w / MP (in the short run, with wage rate w)

name: Cost Minimization Rule
expr: MPL / w = MPK / r

name: Envelope Curve (LAC)
expr: concept: long-run average cost curve is the envelope of all short-run average cost curves

name: Contribution Margin
expr: CM = Selling Price − Variable Cost per unit

name: Perfect Competition
expr: concept: many buyers/sellers, homogeneous product, free entry/exit, firms are price takers

name: Firm's Equilibrium under Perfect Competition
expr: MR = MC = P

name: Monopoly Equilibrium
expr: MR = MC, with P > MC

name: Lerner Index (Degree of Monopoly Power)
expr: L = (P − MC) / P

name: First Degree Price Discrimination
expr: concept: charging each consumer their maximum willingness to pay

name: Second Degree Price Discrimination
expr: concept: charging different prices based on quantity purchased (block pricing)

name: Third Degree Price Discrimination
expr: concept: charging different prices to different market segments

name: Monopolistic Competition
expr: concept: many firms, differentiated products, free entry/exit

name: Excess Capacity under Monopolistic Competition
expr: concept: long-run output is below the minimum-efficient-scale output

name: Cournot Model
expr: concept: oligopoly firms simultaneously choose quantities, assuming rival's output is fixed

name: Bertrand Model
expr: concept: oligopoly firms compete by simultaneously setting prices

name: Stackelberg Model
expr: concept: sequential quantity-setting duopoly with a leader and a follower

name: Kinked Demand Curve
expr: concept: oligopoly demand curve with a kink at the prevailing price, explaining price rigidity

name: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index
expr: HHI = Σ(Si)², sum of squared market shares

name: Concentration Ratio
expr: CRn = sum of market shares of the top n firms

name: Contestable Markets
expr: concept: markets with free entry and exit constrain incumbent pricing even with few firms

name: Natural Monopoly
expr: concept: single firm can supply the entire market at lower cost than multiple firms, due to large economies of scale

name: Monopsony
expr: concept: single buyer in a market, facing an upward-sloping supply curve

name: Bilateral Monopoly
expr: concept: single seller (monopoly) facing single buyer (monopsony)

name: Dominant Firm Price Leadership Model
expr: concept: dominant firm sets price, smaller firms act as price takers

name: Limit Pricing
expr: concept: incumbent sets price low enough to deter entry of new firms

name: Predatory Pricing
expr: concept: firm prices below cost to drive out competitors, then raises price

name: Markup Pricing
expr: P = MC × (1 + markup)

name: Cost-Plus Pricing
expr: P = AC + Markup

name: Deadweight Loss of Monopoly
expr: concept: welfare loss from monopoly output being below the competitive level

name: X-inefficiency
expr: concept: firms not minimizing costs due to lack of competitive pressure

name: Rent Seeking
expr: concept: resources spent to obtain economic gain without creating value

name: Two-Part Tariff
expr: concept: pricing with a fixed entry fee plus a per-unit usage charge

name: GDP – Expenditure Method
expr: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M)

name: GDP – Income Method
expr: GDP = Wages + Rent + Interest + Profit

name: GDP – Output/Value Added Method
expr: GDP = Σ(Value Added at each stage of production)

name: Gross National Product
expr: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad

name: Net National Product
expr: NNP = GNP − Depreciation

name: National Income
expr: NI = NNP at Factor Cost

name: Personal Income
expr: PI = NI − Corporate Profits − Social Security Contributions + Transfer Payments

name: Disposable Personal Income
expr: DPI = PI − Personal Taxes

name: Real GDP
expr: Real GDP = (Nominal GDP / GDP Deflator) × 100

name: GDP Deflator
expr: GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100

name: Per Capita Income
expr: PCI = National Income / Population

name: Value Added
expr: VA = Value of Output − Value of Intermediate Consumption

name: Net Domestic Product
expr: NDP = GDP − Depreciation

name: Consumption Function
expr: C = a + bY

name: Marginal Propensity to Consume
expr: MPC = ΔC / ΔY

name: Marginal Propensity to Save
expr: MPS = ΔS / ΔY

name: MPC + MPS Identity
expr: MPC + MPS = 1

name: Average Propensity to Consume
expr: APC = C / Y

name: Average Propensity to Save
expr: APS = S / Y

name: APC + APS Identity
expr: APC + APS = 1

name: Savings Function
expr: S = Y − C = −a + (1 − b)Y

name: Investment (Keynesian) Multiplier
expr: k = 1 / (1 − MPC) = 1 / MPS

name: Change in Income from Investment
expr: ΔY = k × ΔI

name: Balanced Budget Multiplier
expr: concept: equal increase in government spending and taxes raises income by that same amount, multiplier = 1

name: Double Counting
expr: concept: error of counting the value of intermediate goods more than once in GDP

name: Real GDP Growth Rate
expr: g = [(Real GDPt − Real GDPt-1) / Real GDPt-1] × 100

name: Factor Cost vs Market Price
expr: Market Price = Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes − Subsidies

name: Inflation Rate
expr: Inflation = [(CPIt − CPIt-1) / CPIt-1] × 100

name: Consumer Price Index
expr: CPI = (Cost of Fixed Basket at Current Prices / Cost of Basket at Base Prices) × 100

name: Unemployment Rate
expr: UR = (Number Unemployed / Labor Force) × 100

name: Labor Force Participation Rate
expr: LFPR = (Labor Force / Working-Age Population) × 100

name: Natural Rate of Unemployment
expr: concept: unemployment rate when the economy is at full employment (frictional + structural)

name: Frictional Unemployment
expr: concept: temporary unemployment while workers search for or transition between jobs

name: Structural Unemployment
expr: concept: unemployment due to mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs

name: Cyclical Unemployment
expr: concept: unemployment caused by a downturn in the business cycle

name: Okun's Law
expr: %ΔGDP ≈ 3% − 2 × (Change in Unemployment Rate), approximate rule of thumb

name: Phillips Curve
expr: concept: inverse short-run relationship between inflation and unemployment

name: Misery Index
expr: MI = Inflation Rate + Unemployment Rate

name: Fisher Equation
expr: Nominal Interest Rate = Real Interest Rate + Inflation Rate

name: Real Interest Rate
expr: Real Interest Rate = Nominal Interest Rate − Inflation Rate

name: Purchasing Power Parity
expr: concept: exchange rates adjust so identical goods cost the same across countries

name: Real Exchange Rate
expr: Real Exchange Rate = (Nominal Exchange Rate × Foreign Price Level) / Domestic Price Level

name: Business Cycle
expr: concept: recurring fluctuations of real GDP around its long-run trend

name: Stagflation
expr: concept: simultaneous high inflation and high unemployment with stagnant growth

name: Deflation
expr: concept: sustained fall in the general price level

name: Hyperinflation
expr: concept: extremely rapid and out-of-control general price increases

name: Demand-Pull Inflation
expr: concept: inflation caused by aggregate demand exceeding aggregate supply

name: Cost-Push Inflation
expr: concept: inflation caused by rising production costs

name: Core Inflation
expr: concept: inflation rate excluding volatile items such as food and energy

name: Quantity Theory of Money (Fisher's Equation)
expr: MV = PQ

name: Money Supply
expr: M = Currency in Circulation + Demand Deposits

name: Money Multiplier
expr: m = 1 / Reserve Ratio

name: Velocity of Money
expr: V = PQ / M = Nominal GDP / Money Supply

name: Reserve Ratio
expr: RR = Reserves / Deposits

name: Credit Creation (Deposit) Multiplier
expr: Total Credit Created = Initial Deposit × (1 / RR)

name: Excess Reserves
expr: Excess Reserves = Total Reserves − Required Reserves

name: Open Market Operations
expr: concept: central bank buys/sells government securities to control money supply

name: Discount Rate
expr: concept: interest rate the central bank charges commercial banks for short-term loans

name: Liquidity Preference Theory
expr: concept: interest rate determined by the demand for and supply of money

name: Demand for Money – Transaction Motive
expr: concept: money held to carry out everyday transactions

name: Demand for Money – Precautionary Motive
expr: concept: money held to meet unforeseen expenses

name: Demand for Money – Speculative Motive
expr: concept: money held to take advantage of future investment opportunities

name: Liquidity Trap
expr: concept: situation where interest rates are so low that monetary policy becomes ineffective

name: IS Curve
expr: concept: combinations of interest rate and income where the goods market is in equilibrium

name: LM Curve
expr: concept: combinations of interest rate and income where the money market is in equilibrium

name: IS-LM Equilibrium
expr: concept: interest rate and income level where both goods and money markets clear simultaneously

name: Loanable Funds Theory
expr: concept: interest rate determined by supply of savings and demand for investment funds

name: Monetary Base
expr: MB = Currency in Circulation + Bank Reserves

name: Cash Reserve Ratio
expr: CRR = minimum fraction of deposits banks must hold as reserves with the central bank

name: Statutory Liquidity Ratio
expr: SLR = minimum fraction of deposits banks must hold in liquid assets

name: Interest Rate Parity
expr: concept: interest rate differential between two countries equals the expected exchange rate change

name: Government Budget Balance
expr: Budget Balance = Total Revenue − Total Expenditure

name: Fiscal Deficit
expr: FD = Total Expenditure − Total Revenue (excluding borrowings)

name: Primary Deficit
expr: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments

name: Revenue Deficit
expr: RD = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts

name: Public Debt to GDP Ratio
expr: Debt/GDP = (Total Public Debt / GDP) × 100

name: Tax Multiplier
expr: kt = −MPC / (1 − MPC)

name: Government Spending Multiplier
expr: kg = 1 / (1 − MPC)

name: Average Tax Rate
expr: ATR = Total Tax Paid / Total Income

name: Marginal Tax Rate
expr: MTR = ΔTax / ΔIncome

name: Laffer Curve
expr: concept: relationship suggesting tax revenue can fall if tax rates rise beyond an optimal point

name: Tax Incidence
expr: concept: study of who ultimately bears the burden of a tax

name: Deadweight Loss of Taxation
expr: DWL = ½ × ΔQ × ΔP (welfare loss from the market distortion caused by a tax)

name: Public Goods
expr: concept: goods that are non-excludable and non-rivalrous in consumption

name: Pigouvian Tax
expr: concept: a tax equal to the marginal external cost, used to correct a negative externality

name: Crowding Out Effect
expr: concept: increased government borrowing raises interest rates and reduces private investment

name: Automatic Stabilizers
expr: concept: fiscal tools (like progressive taxes, unemployment benefits) that reduce fluctuations automatically

name: Discretionary Fiscal Policy
expr: concept: deliberate change in government spending or taxes to influence the economy

name: Value Added Tax
expr: VAT Payable = Output Tax − Input Tax

name: Progressive Tax
expr: concept: average tax rate rises as income rises

name: Regressive Tax
expr: concept: average tax rate falls as income rises

name: Proportional Tax
expr: concept: average tax rate stays constant as income rises

name: Balance of Trade
expr: BOT = Exports − Imports

name: Balance of Payments
expr: concept: record of a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world

name: Current Account Balance
expr: concept: net trade in goods/services plus net income and transfers

name: Capital Account Balance
expr: concept: net change in ownership of national assets

name: Absolute Advantage
expr: concept: ability to produce a good using fewer resources than another producer

name: Comparative Advantage
expr: concept: ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another producer

name: Terms of Trade
expr: TOT = (Export Price Index / Import Price Index) × 100

name: Devaluation
expr: concept: deliberate lowering of a currency's value relative to other currencies under a fixed regime

name: Revaluation
expr: concept: deliberate raising of a currency's value relative to other currencies under a fixed regime

name: Marshall-Lerner Condition
expr: concept: devaluation improves trade balance only if sum of export and import demand elasticities exceeds 1

name: J-Curve Effect
expr: concept: trade balance initially worsens then improves following a devaluation

name: Purchasing Power Parity (Exchange Rate)
expr: E = P / P*

name: Effective Rate of Protection
expr: ERP = (VA with tariff − VA without tariff) / VA without tariff

name: Optimal Tariff
expr: concept: tariff rate that maximizes a large country's national welfare by exploiting terms-of-trade gains

name: Infant Industry Argument
expr: concept: case for temporary protection of new domestic industries until they become competitive

name: Trade Deficit
expr: concept: value of imports exceeds value of exports

name: Trade Surplus
expr: concept: value of exports exceeds value of imports

name: Foreign Direct Investment
expr: concept: investment involving a lasting management interest in an enterprise in another country

name: Economic Growth Rate
expr: g = [(GDPt − GDPt-1) / GDPt-1] × 100

name: Harrod-Domar Growth Model
expr: g = s / v (growth rate = savings ratio ÷ capital-output ratio)

name: Solow Growth Model
expr: concept: growth model explaining long-run output growth through capital, labor, and technology

name: Capital-Output Ratio
expr: v = K / Y

name: Steady State
expr: concept: growth path where capital per worker remains constant over time

name: Human Development Index
expr: concept: composite index of life expectancy, education, and income indicators

name: Gini Coefficient
expr: concept: measure of income inequality, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality)

name: Lorenz Curve
expr: concept: graph showing the cumulative share of income earned by cumulative share of population

name: Poverty Headcount Ratio
expr: PHR = (Number of people below the poverty line / Total population) × 100

name: Rostow's Stages of Growth
expr: concept: five-stage model of economic development from traditional society to mass consumption

name: Big Push Theory
expr: concept: large, coordinated investment needed to escape a low-level development trap

name: Lewis Dual Economy Model
expr: concept: development model with labor transfer from a traditional agricultural sector to a modern industrial sector

name: Capital-Labor Ratio
expr: k = K / L

name: Endogenous Growth Theory
expr: concept: long-run growth driven by internal factors such as innovation and human capital, not just external technology

name: Convergence Hypothesis
expr: concept: poorer economies tend to grow faster than richer ones and eventually catch up

name: Incremental Capital Output Ratio
expr: ICOR = Investment / ΔOutput

name: Marginal Revenue Product of Labor
expr: MRPL = MPL × MR

name: Wage Rate under Perfect Competition
expr: W = MRPL

name: Monopsony Wage Determination
expr: concept: monopsonist hires labor where MRP = MFC (marginal factor cost), paying a wage below MRP

name: Efficiency Wage Theory
expr: concept: firms pay above-market wages to boost productivity, loyalty, and reduce turnover

name: Human Capital Theory
expr: concept: education and training are investments that raise a worker's future productivity and earnings

name: Compensating Wage Differential
expr: concept: extra pay required to compensate workers for undesirable job characteristics

name: Real Wage
expr: Real Wage = Nominal Wage / Price Level

name: Dependency Ratio
expr: DR = (Non-working Population / Working Population) × 100

name: Labor Productivity
expr: LP = Total Output / Labor Hours

name: Employment Rate
expr: ER = (Employed / Labor Force) × 100

name: Discouraged Worker Effect
expr: concept: workers stop looking for jobs and exit the labor force during weak job markets

name: Minimum Wage Effect
expr: concept: a binding minimum wage above equilibrium can create excess supply of labor (unemployment)

name: Present Value
expr: PV = FV / (1 + r)^n

name: Future Value
expr: FV = PV × (1 + r)^n

name: Net Present Value
expr: NPV = Σ [CFt / (1 + r)^t] − Initial Investment

name: Internal Rate of Return
expr: concept: discount rate at which NPV of a project equals zero

name: Marginal Efficiency of Capital
expr: concept: expected rate of return on an additional unit of capital investment

name: Accelerator Theory
expr: I = v × ΔY (induced investment is proportional to change in output)

name: Capital Asset Pricing Model
expr: E(Ri) = Rf + βi × (Rm − Rf)

name: Bond Yield
expr: Yield = (Annual Coupon / Price) × 100

name: Rate of Return
expr: RoR = [(Gain − Cost) / Cost] × 100

name: Risk Premium (Finance)
expr: RP = Expected Return − Risk-free Rate

name: Portfolio Return
expr: Rp = Σ (wi × Ri)

name: Payback Period
expr: PP = Initial Investment / Annual Cash Flow

name: Profitability Index
expr: PI = PV of Future Cash Flows / Initial Investment

name: Weighted Average Cost of Capital
expr: WACC = (E/V)×Re + (D/V)×Rd×(1 − Tc)

name: Gordon Growth (Dividend Discount) Model
expr: P = D1 / (r − g)

name: Efficient Market Hypothesis
expr: concept: asset prices fully reflect all available information

name: Simple Linear Regression
expr: Y = a + bX

name: Regression Slope Coefficient
expr: b = Σ(Xi − X̄)(Yi − Ȳ) / Σ(Xi − X̄)²

name: Regression Intercept
expr: a = Ȳ − b·X̄

name: Coefficient of Determination
expr: R² = Explained Variation / Total Variation

name: Correlation Coefficient
expr: r = Cov(X,Y) / (σx × σy)

name: Covariance
expr: Cov(X,Y) = Σ(Xi − X̄)(Yi − Ȳ) / n

name: Multicollinearity
expr: concept: two or more independent variables in a regression are highly correlated with each other

name: Heteroscedasticity
expr: concept: the variance of regression errors is not constant across observations

name: Autocorrelation
expr: concept: regression error terms are correlated across observations, often in time-series data

name: Durbin-Watson Statistic
expr: concept: test statistic used to detect autocorrelation in regression residuals

name: Ordinary Least Squares
expr: concept: estimation method that minimizes the sum of squared residuals

name: Dummy Variable
expr: concept: a variable taking value 0 or 1 used to represent categorical data in regression

name: Log-Linear (Elasticity) Model
expr: ln(Y) = a + b·ln(X), where b is directly the elasticity

name: Index Number
expr: Index = (Value in Given Year / Value in Base Year) × 100

name: Fisher's Ideal Index
expr: FI = √(Laspeyres Index × Paasche Index)

name: Moving Average (Time Series)
expr: concept: average of successive subsets of data, used to smooth short-term fluctuations

name: Mean Absolute Percentage Error
expr: MAPE = (1/n) × Σ |Actual − Forecast| / Actual × 100

name: Nash Equilibrium
expr: concept: a set of strategies where no player can gain by changing their own strategy alone

name: Dominant Strategy
expr: concept: a strategy that gives a player the best outcome regardless of what others do

name: Prisoner's Dilemma
expr: concept: a game showing why two rational players might not cooperate even when it benefits both

name: Zero-Sum Game
expr: concept: one player's gain is exactly equal to another player's loss

name: Minimax Strategy
expr: concept: strategy that minimizes the maximum possible loss

name: Maximin Strategy
expr: concept: strategy that maximizes the minimum possible gain

name: Mixed Strategy
expr: concept: a player randomizes between available strategies according to chosen probabilities

name: Tit-for-Tat Strategy
expr: concept: cooperate first, then mirror the opponent's previous move in repeated games

name: Bounded Rationality
expr: concept: decision-makers have limited information, time, and cognitive ability

name: Anchoring Bias
expr: concept: over-reliance on the first piece of information encountered when making decisions

name: Loss Aversion
expr: concept: losses are felt more strongly than equivalent gains

name: Prospect Theory
expr: concept: describes how people evaluate potential gains and losses relative to a reference point

name: Endowment Effect
expr: concept: people value something more highly simply because they own it

name: Herd Behavior
expr: concept: individuals follow the actions of a larger group rather than their own analysis

name: Time Inconsistency
expr: concept: preferences change over time in a way that conflicts with earlier plans

name: Asymmetric Information
expr: concept: one party in a transaction has more or better information than the other

name: Pareto Efficiency
expr: concept: an allocation where no one can be made better off without making someone else worse off

name: Pareto Improvement
expr: concept: a reallocation that makes at least one person better off without harming anyone else

name: Kaldor-Hicks Efficiency
expr: concept: a change is efficient if gainers could hypothetically compensate losers and still be better off

name: Deadweight Loss (Welfare)
expr: DWL = ½ × ΔQ × ΔP

name: Coase Theorem
expr: concept: with clearly defined property rights and no transaction costs, parties can bargain to an efficient outcome regardless of initial allocation

name: Merit Good
expr: concept: a good that is under-consumed relative to the social optimum if left to the free market

name: Demerit Good
expr: concept: a good that is over-consumed relative to the social optimum if left to the free market

name: Market Failure
expr: concept: situation where the free market fails to allocate resources efficiently

name: Government Failure
expr: concept: situation where government intervention leads to a less efficient outcome than the market

name: Social Cost
expr: Social Cost = Private Cost + External Cost

name: Social Benefit
expr: Social Benefit = Private Benefit + External Benefit

name: Optimal Pigouvian Tax
expr: Optimal Tax = Marginal External Cost at the efficient output level

name: Cobweb Theorem in Agriculture
expr: concept: agricultural prices/output cycle because production decisions are based on past prices

name: Parity Price
expr: concept: price level that maintains a fair relationship between farm prices and other prices in the economy

name: Environmental Kuznets Curve
expr: concept: hypothesis that environmental degradation rises then falls as income per capita increases

name: Carbon Tax
expr: concept: a tax levied per unit of carbon emissions to internalize their external cost

name: Cap and Trade
expr: concept: a system setting a limit on emissions and allowing firms to trade emission permits

name: Sustainable Yield
expr: concept: the maximum rate a renewable resource can be harvested without depleting it over time

name: Green GDP
expr: concept: GDP adjusted to account for environmental degradation and resource depletion

name: Common Property Resource
expr: concept: a resource that is rivalrous but non-excludable, prone to overuse

name: Land Rent (Ricardian Theory)
expr: concept: rent arises from differences in the fertility/productivity of land

name: Break-even Analysis
expr: concept: determining the sales volume at which total revenue equals total cost

name: Operating Leverage
expr: concept: degree to which fixed costs are used in a firm's operations, magnifying profit sensitivity to sales

name: Financial Leverage
expr: concept: degree to which debt financing is used, magnifying the effect of earnings on shareholder returns

name: Demand Forecasting
expr: concept: estimating future demand for a product using historical data and market analysis

name: Shadow Price
expr: concept: the implicit value of a resource, especially in constrained optimization problems

name: Sensitivity Analysis
expr: concept: examining how changes in key assumptions affect a decision's outcome

name: Decision Tree Analysis
expr: concept: diagram-based method for evaluating decisions with uncertain outcomes

name: Expected Monetary Value
expr: EMV = Σ (Probability × Payoff)

name: Cost-Benefit Analysis
expr: Benefit-Cost Ratio = PV of Benefits / PV of Costs

name: Aggregate Demand
expr: AD = C + I + G + (X − M)

name: Aggregate Supply (Short Run)
expr: concept: total output firms are willing to supply at each price level, given sticky wages/prices

name: Aggregate Supply (Long Run)
expr: concept: vertical at potential/full-employment output, independent of the price level

name: AD-AS Equilibrium
expr: concept: price level and real output where aggregate demand equals aggregate supply

name: Potential Output (Full Employment GDP)
expr: concept: the maximum sustainable output an economy can produce using all resources efficiently

name: Output Gap
expr: Output Gap = Actual GDP − Potential GDP

name: Say's Law
expr: concept: 'supply creates its own demand' — production generates enough income to purchase all output

name: Keynesian Cross Model
expr: concept: equilibrium income determined where planned aggregate expenditure equals actual output

name: Paradox of Thrift
expr: concept: an increase in planned saving can reduce aggregate demand and lower actual income/saving

name: Multiplier-Accelerator Interaction
expr: concept: combined effect of the income multiplier and investment accelerator, generating business cycles

name: Real Business Cycle Theory
expr: concept: business cycles driven mainly by real shocks such as technology, not monetary factors

name: Monetarism
expr: concept: school emphasizing control of money supply growth as the key to price stability

name: New Classical Economics
expr: concept: school emphasizing rational expectations and market-clearing prices

name: New Keynesian Economics
expr: concept: school emphasizing sticky prices/wages that justify active stabilization policy

name: Riba (Interest) Prohibition
expr: concept: prohibition of predetermined, fixed interest on loans in Islamic economics

name: Zakat Calculation
expr: Zakat = 2.5% × (Zakatable Wealth above Nisab, held for one lunar year)

name: Nisab Threshold
expr: concept: minimum amount of wealth a Muslim must own before zakat becomes obligatory

name: Mudarabah Profit Sharing
expr: Profit Share = Agreed Ratio × Total Profit (loss borne by capital provider only)

name: Musharakah (Partnership) Profit-Loss Sharing
expr: Profit shared per agreed ratio; Loss shared strictly in proportion to capital contribution

name: Murabaha (Cost-Plus Sale)
expr: Selling Price = Cost Price + Disclosed Profit Margin

name: Ijarah (Leasing)
expr: concept: asset ownership stays with lessor; lessee pays rent for usufruct of the asset

name: Sukuk (Islamic Bond) Return
expr: concept: return linked to profit/rental income from an underlying tangible asset, not fixed interest

name: Gharar (Excessive Uncertainty) Prohibition
expr: concept: contracts with excessive ambiguity or risk are not permissible

name: Qard-e-Hasan (Benevolent Loan)
expr: concept: interest-free loan repaid at the same nominal amount as borrowed

name: Takaful (Islamic Insurance)
expr: concept: participants contribute to a mutual fund used to compensate members who suffer loss

name: Ushr
expr: Ushr = 10% × Produce (on rain-fed land) or 5% × Produce (on irrigated land)

name: Profit Equalization Reserve
expr: concept: reserve set aside by Islamic banks to smooth depositor returns across periods

name: Diminishing Musharakah
expr: concept: partner's share in a jointly owned asset is bought out gradually by the other partner over time

name: Health Production Function
expr: Health = f(Medical Care, Income, Education, Lifestyle, Environment)

name: Demand for Health Care
expr: concept: health care demand is largely a derived demand for better health

name: Moral Hazard in Health Insurance
expr: concept: insured individuals consume more healthcare because they bear a lower share of the cost

name: Adverse Selection in Insurance Markets
expr: concept: higher-risk individuals are more likely to buy insurance, raising average costs

name: Quality-Adjusted Life Year
expr: QALY = Years of Life × Quality-of-Life Weight (0 to 1)

name: Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (Health)
expr: CER = Cost of Treatment / Health Outcome Achieved

name: Out-of-Pocket Health Expenditure Ratio
expr: OOP Ratio = (Out-of-Pocket Health Spending / Total Health Spending) × 100

name: Elasticity of Demand for Health Care
expr: concept: typically low/inelastic, especially for essential or emergency care

name: Rate of Return to Education
expr: concept: increase in lifetime earnings attributable to an additional year of schooling

name: Human Capital Accumulation
expr: concept: process of increasing productive knowledge and skills through education and training

name: Signaling Model of Education
expr: concept: education signals worker ability to employers, rather than only raising productivity

name: Education Production Function
expr: Learning Outcome = f(School Inputs, Family Background, Student Ability)

name: Gross Enrolment Ratio
expr: GER = (Total Enrolment in a Level / Population of the Relevant Age Group) × 100

name: Net Enrolment Ratio
expr: NER = (Enrolment of Official Age Group in a Level / Population of that Age Group) × 100

name: Bid-Rent Curve
expr: concept: land rent that a land use is willing to pay, falling as distance from the city center increases

name: Location Quotient
expr: LQ = (Local Industry Employment / Local Total Employment) ÷ (National Industry Employment / National Total Employment)

name: Agglomeration Economies
expr: concept: cost savings that arise when firms and workers cluster together in one location

name: Urbanization Rate
expr: Urbanization Rate = (Urban Population / Total Population) × 100

name: Central Place Theory
expr: concept: theory explaining the size, number, and location of cities/towns in a region

name: Crude Birth Rate
expr: CBR = (Number of Live Births / Total Population) × 1000

name: Crude Death Rate
expr: CDR = (Number of Deaths / Total Population) × 1000

name: Rate of Natural Increase
expr: RNI = Crude Birth Rate − Crude Death Rate

name: Total Fertility Rate
expr: concept: average number of children a woman would have over her reproductive years at current fertility rates

name: Demographic Dividend
expr: concept: economic growth potential from a rising share of working-age population relative to dependents

name: Malthusian Theory of Population
expr: concept: population grows geometrically while food supply grows arithmetically, causing periodic checks

name: Median Voter Theorem
expr: concept: in majority voting, the outcome reflects the preference of the median voter

name: Rent Seeking (Public Choice)
expr: concept: use of resources to obtain economic gain through political/regulatory means rather than production

name: Logrolling
expr: concept: trading votes among legislators to secure passage of mutually preferred bills

name: Bureaucratic Inefficiency (Public Choice)
expr: concept: government agencies may over-produce output relative to the social optimum due to budget-maximizing incentives

name: Free Rider Problem
expr: concept: individuals benefit from a public good without contributing to its cost

name: Classical Economics
expr: concept: school (Smith, Ricardo) emphasizing free markets, the 'invisible hand', and limited government role

name: Keynesian Economics
expr: concept: school emphasizing aggregate demand management to stabilize output and employment

name: Marxian Economics
expr: concept: school analyzing capitalism through class conflict, surplus value, and labor exploitation

name: Neoclassical Economics
expr: concept: school built on marginal utility, rational optimization, and market equilibrium

name: Austrian School
expr: concept: school emphasizing individual choice, market processes, and skepticism of central planning

name: Institutional Economics
expr: concept: school emphasizing the role of institutions, norms, and legal structures in shaping economic outcomes

name: Elasticity of Demand for Imports
expr: concept: responsiveness of import quantity to changes in import price

name: Elasticity of Demand for Exports
expr: concept: responsiveness of export quantity to changes in export price

name: Cross-Price Elasticity Matrix
expr: concept: table of cross elasticities among all pairs of goods in a consumer's basket

name: Composite Elasticity (Multi-market)
expr: concept: combined elasticity effect when a price change affects several related markets

name: Bertrand Paradox
expr: concept: with identical products and no capacity limits, just two price-competing firms can reach the competitive outcome

name: Sweezy (Kinked Demand) Model
expr: concept: alternative name for the kinked demand curve model of oligopoly price rigidity

name: Collusion (Tacit vs Explicit)
expr: concept: firms coordinate pricing/output either through informal understanding or formal agreement

name: Segmented Labor Market
expr: concept: labor market divided into distinct segments (e.g., primary/secondary) with limited mobility between them

name: Union Wage Premium
expr: concept: wage gap between unionized and non-unionized workers with similar characteristics

name: Bilateral Monopoly in Labor Market
expr: concept: wage outcome negotiated between a single employer (monopsonist) and a single union (monopoly seller of labor)

name: Chi-Square Test
expr: concept: statistical test used to assess association between categorical economic variables

name: F-test (Overall Regression Significance)
expr: F = (Explained Variance / k) ÷ (Unexplained Variance / (n−k−1))

name: Human Capital Investment
expr: concept: spending on education/training that raises future productivity and earnings

name: Signaling Theory
expr: concept: informed party takes a costly, observable action to credibly convey private information

name: Screening
expr: concept: uninformed party designs mechanisms to induce informed parties to reveal private information

name: Moral Hazard
expr: concept: a party takes on more risk because the costs are borne by another party

name: Principal-Agent Problem
expr: concept: conflict of interest between a principal and an agent acting on their behalf

name: Transaction Cost Economics
expr: concept: analysis of the costs of participating in a market, influencing firm and contract structure

name: Property Rights Theory
expr: concept: how the allocation of ownership rights affects resource use and economic efficiency

name: Rational Expectations Hypothesis
expr: concept: individuals form expectations using all available information efficiently, without systematic error

name: Adaptive Expectations Hypothesis
expr: concept: individuals form expectations based on past values and gradually adjust to errors

name: Ricardian Equivalence
expr: concept: consumers anticipate future taxes from government borrowing and save accordingly, offsetting fiscal stimulus

name: Crowding In Effect
expr: concept: government spending can raise expected future profitability and encourage more private investment

name: Debt Servicing Ratio
expr: DSR = (Debt Service Payments / Export Earnings) × 100

name: Gross Fixed Capital Formation
expr: concept: value of acquisitions of fixed assets by producers, less disposals, in a period

name: Wagner's Law
expr: concept: government expenditure tends to rise as an economy industrializes and per capita income grows

name: Baumol's Cost Disease
expr: concept: costs in labor-intensive sectors with low productivity growth rise faster than the economy-wide average

name: Hicksian Demand Function
expr: concept: quantity demanded that minimizes expenditure for a given level of utility

name: Marshallian Demand Function
expr: concept: quantity demanded that maximizes utility for a given level of income and prices

name: Shephard's Lemma
expr: concept: the derivative of the expenditure function with respect to price gives the Hicksian demand

name: Roy's Identity
expr: concept: derives Marshallian demand from the indirect utility function

name: Slutsky Symmetry
expr: concept: cross-price substitution effects between two goods are symmetric

name: Homothetic Preferences
expr: concept: preferences where the ratio of goods demanded stays constant as income scales up

name: Quasilinear Utility Function
expr: concept: utility function linear in one good, with no income effect on the demand for that good

name: Marginal Rate of Transformation
expr: MRT = ΔY / ΔX, along the production possibility frontier

name: Production Possibility Frontier Slope
expr: concept: PPF slope represents the opportunity cost of producing one more unit of a good

name: Law of Comparative Costs
expr: concept: countries should specialize in goods where their opportunity cost is lowest

name: Absolute vs Comparative Advantage Distinction
expr: concept: absolute advantage compares productivity, comparative advantage compares opportunity cost

name: Gains from Trade
expr: concept: increase in total consumption possible when countries specialize and trade based on comparative advantage

name: Infant Mortality Rate
expr: IMR = (Deaths under age 1 / Live Births) × 1000

name: Literacy Rate
expr: Literacy Rate = (Literate Population / Total Population aged 15+) × 100

name: Real vs Nominal Variables
expr: concept: nominal values are measured in current prices, real values are adjusted for inflation

name: Base Year Selection (Index Numbers)
expr: concept: a normal, representative year chosen as the reference point (=100) for an index series

name: Chain-Linked Index
expr: concept: index constructed by linking successive period-to-period indices rather than a fixed base year

name: Seasonal Adjustment
expr: concept: removing regular, predictable seasonal patterns from a time series to reveal the underlying trend

name: Forecast Error
expr: Forecast Error = Actual Value − Forecasted Value

name: Marginal Social Cost
expr: MSC = Marginal Private Cost + Marginal External Cost

name: Marginal Social Benefit
expr: MSB = Marginal Private Benefit + Marginal External Benefit

name: Socially Optimal Output
expr: concept: output level where Marginal Social Benefit equals Marginal Social Cost

name: Command Economy
expr: concept: economic system where government decides what, how, and for whom to produce

name: Market Economy
expr: concept: economic system where prices and private decisions allocate resources

name: Mixed Economy
expr: concept: economic system combining market forces with government intervention

name: Command vs Market Efficiency Trade-off
expr: concept: markets tend to be more efficient at resource allocation, command systems may better address equity goals

name: Structural Adjustment Program
expr: concept: policy reforms (often IMF/World Bank linked) aimed at correcting macroeconomic imbalances

name: Foreign Exchange Reserves Adequacy
expr: Reserve Adequacy (months) = Foreign Exchange Reserves / Average Monthly Imports

name: Current Account Deficit to GDP Ratio
expr: CAD/GDP = (Current Account Deficit / GDP) × 100

name: Export-Led Growth Strategy
expr: concept: development strategy focused on expanding exports as the main driver of economic growth

name: Import Substitution Industrialization
expr: concept: development strategy of replacing imports with domestically produced goods

name: Terms of Trade Deterioration
expr: concept: a fall in the ratio of export prices to import prices over time, common concern for primary-good exporters

name: Dutch Disease
expr: concept: a resource boom appreciates the currency and harms competitiveness of other export sectors

name: Resource Curse
expr: concept: countries rich in natural resources sometimes experiencing slower growth and weaker institutions

name: Vicious Circle of Poverty
expr: concept: low income leads to low savings and investment, which perpetuates low income

name: Absolute Income Hypothesis
expr: concept: current consumption depends mainly on current absolute income level

name: Permanent Income Hypothesis
expr: concept: consumption depends on a household's expected long-run (permanent) income, not just current income
